title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Top Support Issues
author: Ariana Chen
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines standards, templates, and operational procedures that the Developer Experience (DevEx) team uses to produce SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is consistent, discoverable, and high-quality docs that reduce onboarding time, decrease support load, and make SDK + API usage in Redwood products predictable and reliable.

Audience:
- SDK authors, technical writers, and solutions engineers
- Support engineers and on-call responders
- Product and platform engineers who ship public API changes

Principles:
- Keep examples copy-pasteable: small, complete, and minimal external dependencies.
- Single source of truth: API examples live in the docs repo and are CI-checked.
- Fast iteration: docs must be editable with a clear PR + review flow and automated validation.
- Observable impact: track top search terms and support ticket causes; prioritize documentation improvements by actual user pain.

Required doc types and minimum metadata (every page):
1. Title, short description (1–2 sentences), and audience
2. Examples: at least one language example (Python or JavaScript) and one curl snippet
3. Code block with installation instructions and a running example
4. Troubleshooting / common errors with diagnostic commands
5. Owner + reviewers + last updated date

Templates (use these as starting points):
- SDK Guide Template (file: sdk-guide-template.md):
  1. Overview (what this SDK covers and supported versions)
  2. Quick install (pip/npm) + compatibility table (runtime, supported models)
  3. Auth pattern and best practices (token rotation, KMS link)
  4. Basic usage examples (init client, text generation, streaming)
  5. Advanced topics (batching, caching integration, async usage)
  6. Error handling and retry semantics (HTTP codes, idempotency guidance)
  7. Tests and CI checks (how to run snippets in CI)
  8. Changelog and migration notes

- Quickstart Template (file: quickstart-template.md):
  - Goal: brief one-line objective
  - Prereqs: account, API key, region
  - Steps (numbered):
    1) Install SDK or use curl
    2) Minimal auth + run example (complete program)
    3) Verify (expected output)
    4) Next steps (link to SDK Guide, full examples)
  - Time to complete: 5–10 minutes

- API Example Pattern:
  - Provide these three variants for every endpoint: curl, Python, JavaScript.
  - In-code comments should explain common parameters and SLO trade-offs (latency/cost).
  - Include a streaming snippet if endpoint supports streaming.
  - Keep examples idempotent and avoid hard-coded secrets.

Canonical SDK Quickstart (example content):
- Prereqs: Redwood account, API key in REDWOOD_API_KEY environment variable
- Install (Python): pip install redwood-inference
- Example (Python):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), region='us-west1')
  resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood-alpha-1', prompt='Write a short haiku about distributed systems')
  print(resp.text)

- Example (curl):
  curl -X POST 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","prompt":"Hello world"}'

Docs Site Operating Procedures (roles and steps):
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/docs-site (canonical location for content)
- Branching and PRs:
  - All content changes go through feature branches and PRs targeted at main.
  - PR should include: preview URL, short summary of change, list of affected pages, and screenshots for UI changes.
  - Small doc fixes (typo/clarity) may be merged by the owner; substantive changes require one reviewer from DevEx and one from product/engineering if the change affects API behavior.
- CI checks (automated):
  - Markdown linting and link checking
  - Snippet execution tests: run language snippet tests in a sandbox (CI uses a read-only API key)
  - Accessibility checks for images/alt text
- Release schedule:
  - Docs are deployed continuously; a single-site production deploy occurs daily at 02:00 UTC for non-breaking updates. Breaking changes (API contract changes) should be coordinated with releases and indicated in release notes.
- Rollback: revert the PR and re-deploy. For urgent customer-facing regressions, follow the incident runbook and notify support and product.

Owner matrix and SLAs for doc changes:
- Page owner: named in the page metadata. Responsible for ensuring content accuracy and triaging doc-related bugs.
- DevEx on-call (rotating): monitors docs-site errors and search trends; action SLA: 48h for severity-high typos or broken examples; 5 business days for non-critical improvements.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (living list) — include in the docs-site section "Top Issues" and link to canonical fixes. Keep the list prioritized by weekly ticket volume.
1) Symptom: Authentication failures with 401 when using SDKs
   Root cause: Users copy the example with a placeholder API key or the environment variable isn't exported correctly
   Canonical fix: Add explicit export and verification step to quickstart. Example: 
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk-live-..."
   python -c "import os; print(bool(os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')))"
   Owner: DevEx - Samir Patel
2) Symptom: Streaming responses appear truncated in client apps
   Root cause: Client did not consume stream events to completion or closed connection on first chunk
   Canonical fix: Provide streaming consumption pattern in SDK guides and an example reconnection strategy. Note the server-side idle timeout is 60s for streaming sessions.
   Owner: eng-serving-runtime - Jonas Berg
3) Symptom: High request latency when using batch endpoints
   Root cause: Incorrect batching size or using small requests that disable efficient batching kernels
   Canonical fix: Add guidance table with recommended batch size per model and example code to group requests server-side. Include metrics to monitor: p50/p95 latency and tokens/sec.
   Owner: eng-serving-runtime - Performance team
4) Symptom: Mismatched model versions between SDK defaults and deployed model catalog
   Root cause: SDK pinned default to a legacy model name after a catalog rename
   Canonical fix: Enforce catalog cross-check in CI and add a post-deploy doc validation that warns on default-version drift.
   Owner: product - Model Catalog
5) Symptom: Examples fail in restricted corporate networks
   Root cause: Default examples use public endpoints and do not demonstrate private deployment (VPC) usage
   Canonical fix: Add a private-deployment quickstart (VPC + proxy) and include troubleshooting steps for proxy env variables (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY).
   Owner: eng-private-deployments - Onboarding team

Troubleshooting checklist for support engineers (quick):
- Verify API key: run env check (python -c ...).
- Confirm region and endpoint: ensure sample is pointing to the customer's region (us-west1 / eu-central1).
- Reproduce with curl: if curl works, the issue is SDK-level; collect SDK version, OS, and full request/response.
- Check SDK changelog and model catalog version: run sdk --version and list models.
- If streaming: capture first N frames and server-side logs (attach to ticket).

Testing and CI guidance for doc authors:
- Snippet tests: add a test under docs/snippets/tests/ that runs the example with a sandbox key. CI will mark broken examples as failed PR checks.
- Lint rules: adhere to markdown styleguide (prose length, H2 usage, code fence language tags).
- Automated metrics: pages with >10 searches/month for unresolved queries are prioritized for improvement.

Maintenance cadence and review process:
- Quarterly content review: owners receive a reminder to review critical guides (SDK, auth, quickstarts) every 90 days.
- Post-release review: for any API change, owners must update code examples and add migration notes within one week of the release.

Appendix: Example PR checklist for documentation changes:
1) Title describes the change and target page(s)
2) Links to preview URL
3) Include snippet tests or marked N/A if purely editorial
4) Update owners/reviewers if responsibility changes
5) Add labels: docs, release-impact (yes/no), module (sdk/js/python)

Related resources:
- Developer Experience docs-site (canonical): /eng-developer-experience/docs-site
- SDK repos: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python and /sdk-js
- Model catalog and runtime docs: /eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture

Contact and escalation:
- Primary Doc Owner (DevEx): Ariana Chen (ariana@redwood.ai)
- DevEx On-call (support triage): devex-oncall@redwood.ai
- Escalation to SRE/Product if docs reveal a runtime bug: create an incident and tag runbook `docs->runtime`

Last reviewed notes:
- 2026-02-10: Added "Top support issues" section and streaming reconnection guidance (reviewers: Samir Patel, Jonas Berg).

End of playbook.
